summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: MoneyGram taps stablecoin ally
articles.description: The cross-border company and its rival Western Union are both working with Signify Holdings, aka Rain, to power new digital currency ventures.

articles.title: Scammers fake student identities to siphon aid payments
articles.description: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network is warning payment processors and financial institutions “to be vigilant” of the fraud schemes.

articles.title: Clarity Act bill stumbles
articles.description: A measure to regulate crypto assets and stablecoin payments failed in the Senate. Regulators now may have to forge a blueprint for the sector.

articles.title: House passes Common Cents bill
articles.description: The bill officially ends minting of pennies and allows merchants to round to the nearest nickel, though the coins are already out of production. It’s the second time the chamber has taken up such legislation.

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard settle Grubhub case
articles.description: The final settlements in a federal lawsuit over credit card swipe fees, led by the food delivery company, came on the eve of a trial in Chicago.

articles.title: Trade groups knock BNPL rules
articles.description: The American Fintech Council argues that New York’s proposed buy now, pay later rules could slash credit available to the state’s consumers.

articles.title: Mastercard CFO seeks int’l growth
articles.description: The company’s new chief financial officer presented his view of stablecoins, growth and acquisitions at an investment bank conference last week.

articles.title: Walmart slams card fee pact, again
articles.description: The largest U.S. retailer joined hundreds of other merchants calling a swipe-fee settlement with the card networks inadequate and unfair.
